name: The Printed Record
summary: A print-first evidence identity that makes one central finding readable while retaining its denominator and method.

palette.name: Background
palette.evidence: Native Office page/sheet white ground; explicit design choice retaining the reading surface.

palette.name: Text
palette.evidence: used style Normal explicit text color

palette.name: Evidence header
palette.evidence: Native reference.docx word/document.xml active shading/border value #333333; source visual and native-design-style-audit corroboration.

palette.name: Evidence row
palette.evidence: Native reference.docx word/document.xml active shading/border value #F2F5F7; source visual and native-design-style-audit corroboration.

typography.usage: Titles and short section openings; source used style Title.
Reading text, supporting labels and detailed explanations; source used style Subtitle.

recognitionRules: Give the principal finding a strong Arial headline with its denominator intact; use Cambria for the reading paragraphs.
Use Arial section headings and Cambria narrative text, retaining table headers and explicit count labels.
Keep a visible How this brief was made section.
Use monochrome rules and spacing rather than color to separate evidence from interpretation.

principles: Move from observation to interpretation to a bounded next question.
Use the identity’s sample as a rhythm and vocabulary reference, not as a factual project claim.
voice.sample: A useful number comes with the count behind it.
voice.sampleStatus: Original fictional brand copy authored for this guide, not a quotation or factual claim.
avoid: Avoid “proves” when the material only supports a hypothesis.
Avoid invented testimonials, performance claims and quotation attribution.
voice.secondaryExample: A record suggests a direction; it does not speak for every person.
voice.cadence: Short opening, concrete follow-through; vary sentence length for explanation.

logoDirection: Use THE PRINTED RECORD in Cambria with a thin baseline rule and a small issue date. No chart icon or numerical badge.
invariants: Give the principal finding a strong Arial headline with its denominator intact; use Cambria for the reading paragraphs.
Use Arial section headings and Cambria narrative text, retaining table headers and explicit count labels.
Keep a visible How this brief was made section.
adaptations: A wall extract retains the denominator and source note.
Longer findings move detail into a separate evidence page.
Keep the full name with any new symbol until the audience can recognize it independently.

fonts.sourceFontDependency: Arial is a separately licensed Microsoft/system font; not bundled.
Cambria is a separately licensed Microsoft/Office font; not bundled.

clearSpaceRule: Keep one half of the main wordmark cap height clear around the full silhouette, including its source-derived supporting device.

minimumSize.status: production minimum based on rendered 220/180px wordmark and 32/64px symbol inspection; verify again for unusual substrates
